Russian UAT-11795 Trojanizes WebEx and Zoom Installers to Deploy Starland RAT


Jul 16, 10:19


A financially motivated Russian threat actor tracked as UAT-11795 is distributing trojanized versions of WebEx and Zoom installation packages that deliver a new backdoor called Starland RAT, designed to steal credentials and cryptocurrency. The campaign targets users downloading enterprise collaboration software from unofficial sources. This follows the Zoom critical Windows CVE patched this week — the dual threat of a legitimate Zoom vulnerability and fake trojanized Zoom installers creates compounding risk.


Trojanized versions of the two most widely deployed enterprise video conferencing tools, actively distributing credential and crypto stealers, is an immediate user awareness and download policy issue.


Sources: BleepingComputer


Spirals Ransomware Completes Full Corporate Compromise — Initial Access to Encryption — in Under 24 Hours


Jul 16, 10:00


A new ransomware operation called Spirals has demonstrated the ability to complete an entire corporate intrusion cycle — from initial access through data exfiltration to full network encryption — in less than 24 hours. The sub-24-hour dwell time eliminates most traditional detection windows that rely on behavioral anomaly analysis over days. The operation is newly identified, meaning defensive signatures and threat intelligence coverage are limited.


Sub-24-hour ransomware that outpaces typical detection and response windows changes incident response planning assumptions — dwell-time-dependent detection strategies are insufficient against this tempo.


Sources: BleepingComputer


Kratos PhaaS Targets Microsoft 365 Accounts Globally with Believable Document and Invoice Lures


Jul 16, 09:16


Kratos is a phishing-as-a-service platform purpose-built to steal Microsoft 365 credentials, targeting organizations across the US, Europe, and other regions using document, invoice, and file-sharing lures that redirect to convincing fake login pages. The platform lowers the barrier for credential theft campaigns against M365 environments, which remain the dominant enterprise identity target. Coverage spans small businesses, law firms, schools, and industrial organizations.


A commoditized PhaaS platform specifically engineered for M365 credential theft at global scale is a direct threat to any organization using Microsoft 365 as its primary productivity suite.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


TuxBot v3 IoT Botnet Uses LLM-Generated Exploit Code to Hijack Routers and Cameras for DDoS


Jul 16, 08:29


A newly identified IoT botnet framework called TuxBot v3 Evolution uses LLM-generated code to attack internet-connected Linux devices across multiple hardware architectures, converting compromised routers, cameras, and embedded systems into DDoS infrastructure. The use of LLM-generated exploit code enables the botnet to target a wider range of device types without requiring custom development for each architecture. This is among the first documented cases of LLM-generated code being used operationally in botnet malware.


LLM-generated code enabling cross-architecture IoT botnet targeting is a new capability milestone — it extends the attack surface for DDoS infrastructure to virtually any Linux-based networked device.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


China's Top Cybersecurity Firms Face Military Procurement Bans — Geopolitical Risk Hits Domestic Vendors


Jul 16, 08:49


China's People's Liberation Army is banning procurement from some of China's largest domestic cybersecurity companies, a development that is not attributed to product failures but appears driven by political and security vetting concerns. The bans affect firms that had positioned themselves as trusted suppliers to Chinese government and military customers. The development signals internal fractures in China's technology supply chain trust model.


Military procurement bans on Chinese cybersecurity vendors reshapes the domestic Chinese security market and is a significant geopolitical signal about trust dynamics within China's own technology ecosystem.


Sources: SecurityWeek


AI & Machine Learning


OpenAI GPT-Red: Automated AI Red-Teamer Scales Prompt Injection Discovery — Used to Harden GPT-5.6 Sol


Jul 16, 08:42


OpenAI has disclosed that GPT-Red, an internal automated red-teaming model, was used extensively to harden GPT-5.6 Sol by discovering and fixing prompt injection vulnerabilities at a scale impossible for human red-teamers. OpenAI states that previous models were 'highly vulnerable' to GPT-Red's attacks, and that GPT-Red is now a continuous adversarial training component. The disclosure confirms that AI-vs-AI adversarial evaluation is now a standard part of OpenAI's model hardening pipeline.


Automated AI adversarial red-teaming as standard practice — and OpenAI's admission that prior models were highly vulnerable to it — is a direct signal about the prompt injection attack surface of deployed AI systems.


Sources: The Hacker News · Cybersecurity News


Meta Adds Parental Alerts When Teens Discuss Suicide or Self-Harm with Its AI Chatbot


Jul 16, 11:00


Meta announced that its AI chatbot will now notify parents when a teenager raises topics related to suicide or self-harm in a conversation, a direct response to regulatory scrutiny and pressure from parents and safety advocates about AI chatbots interacting with minors in crisis. The feature represents a significant policy shift from Meta's previous stance on AI chatbot privacy and parental visibility. It arrives as multiple jurisdictions are moving toward mandated AI safety requirements for minors.

Cyber Security

Researchers at Hacktron tasked GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, Sol Medium, and Grok 4.5 with a real offensive security challenge: construct a working exploit chain for Chrome's V8 engine using only publicly available security-fix commits as input. GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra succeeded, independently producing a complete, functional exploit chain with no other assistance. The finding establishes a new benchmark for AI-assisted vulnerability research and marks a qualitative shift in what frontier models can do offensively.


An AI that can reverse-engineer a working browser exploit from patch diffs alone fundamentally changes the threat modeling equation — every patch release now potentially arms AI-assisted attackers.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


Zoom Critical Account Takeover Vulnerability — Unauthenticated Attacker Can Hijack Accounts via Windows Client


Jul 15, 20:16


Zoom disclosed a critical vulnerability in its Windows desktop client and SDK that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to take over user accounts. The flaw affects the widely-deployed enterprise collaboration platform used by hundreds of millions. Zoom has released patches and users should update immediately.


A critical unauthenticated account takeover in Zoom's Windows client is a high-urgency patch for any organization where Zoom is a primary collaboration tool — attacker access to Zoom accounts means access to meetings, recordings, and integrated workflows.

Identity Attacks Overtake Exploits as Top Ransomware Root Cause — MFA Failed in 97% of Credential Attacks


Jul 15, 20:16


New industry data shows that email-based identity attacks have displaced vulnerability exploitation as the leading ransomware initial access vector, with credential compromise now the dominant entry path. Most alarmingly, MFA was deployed in 97% of credential-based attacks but failed to prevent compromise in the majority of cases — indicating that standard MFA implementations are being routinely bypassed via session hijacking, adversary-in-the-middle proxies, and fatigue attacks.


MFA failing in nearly all credential-based ransomware attacks means the standard enterprise security control that most organizations rely on as their primary credential defense is no longer sufficient on its own.

Jul 15, 17:15


Threat actors are running Google Ads targeting searches for 'claude download' and 'claude mac,' redirecting victims to sites that deliver MacSync Stealer, a macOS infostealer, according to Zscaler. The campaign exploits both Google's ad platform and Anthropic's brand recognition, using shared Claude chat links to add legitimacy. Mac users who downloaded Claude from a Google ad in the past window should audit their systems.


Malvertising campaigns abusing a major AI brand to deliver macOS infostealers are directly targeting the developer and security community that most uses Claude — a high-value credential and credential harvesting target.


Sources: Cybersecurity News

Jul 15, 21:19


Security researchers disclosed that nearly a dozen vulnerable UEFI shim bootloaders that should have been revoked remained trusted by Secure Boot for years, giving attackers a path to bypass firmware-level boot integrity protections. The issue affects organizations that rely on Secure Boot as a defense against persistent firmware implants and bootkits. The finding is particularly relevant given the elevated threat environment following the record July Patch Tuesday.


Secure Boot bypass via forgotten trusted bootloaders undermines one of the most fundamental firmware security guarantees — relevant for any organization using Secure Boot as a control against advanced persistent threats.


Sources: Dark Reading


Dutch Police Bust €100M+ International Investment Fraud Ring with Tens of Thousands of Victims


Jul 15, 21:55


Dutch police announced the arrest of multiple individuals tied to an international investment fraud scheme that stole more than €100 million from tens of thousands of victims. The operation follows the Spanish police takedown of a €140M BEC and investment fraud ring documented in the previous brief — two major European law enforcement actions against financial cybercrime in consecutive days. Investment fraud targeting retail victims remains one of the highest-volume cybercrime categories globally.


Two major European investment fraud enforcement actions in 48 hours signals coordinated international law enforcement pressure on financial cybercrime infrastructure across the continent.


Sources: BleepingComputer

Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Releases Inkling — 975B-Parameter Open Multimodal Model with Anti-Censorship Design


Jul 15, 18:04


Thinking Machines Lab, founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, released Inkling, a 975-billion-parameter open-weights multimodal MoE model under Apache 2.0 license, capable of reasoning across text, images, and audio. Mira Murati's first public model is the most significant new open-weights release from a credentialed US AI lab in months — it's a direct alternative to closed frontier models for enterprises needing on-premises control.


Sources: TechCrunch · VentureBeat · Wired


OpenAI Builds GPT-Red — An LLM Super-Hacker Used to Harden Its Own Models Against Cyberattacks


Jul 15, 17:09


OpenAI has developed an internal LLM called GPT-Red designed specifically to function as a cyber-offensive adversary, used as a sparring partner to stress-test and harden production models. GPT-5.6 was trained against GPT-Red, which OpenAI says made it the most robust release yet. The approach treats AI red-teaming as an automated, continuous process rather than a periodic human exercise.


Automated AI-vs-AI adversarial hardening is a new paradigm for model safety — it also means OpenAI has built and operates a highly capable offensive AI system internally.


Sources: MIT Technology Review


Google Gemini CLI Weaponized as Hacking Agent and Botnet Operator by Russian Threat Actor


Jul 15, 18:33


A Russian-speaking threat actor known as 'bandcampro' used Google's open-source Gemini CLI tool as a core hacking agent and to operate a small-scale botnet, according to BleepingComputer. The actor embedded Gemini CLI directly into offensive operations rather than using it as a research aid. This follows the Chinese state actor case documented in the previous brief that used Claude Code and DeepSeek in espionage campaigns — the pattern of commercial AI CLI tools being weaponized in real attacks is now multi-actor.


A second independent case of a commercial AI CLI tool being used as a live hacking agent — now by a Russian actor — confirms this is a repeatable attack pattern, not an isolated incident.


Sources: BleepingComputer

Jul 16, 02:34


New research documented in the NYT finds that violent extremist groups including Boko Haram are using AI chatbots operationally — for bomb construction guidance and attack planning — not merely as propaganda generation tools. The research represents some of the most concrete evidence to date that AI is being integrated into the actual execution layer of terrorist operations. The findings have significant implications for AI provider trust and safety policies and government monitoring frameworks.


AI-assisted terrorist attack planning is a qualitative escalation from AI-generated propaganda — it reframes the policy debate around AI access controls and monitoring from content moderation to operational security.


Sources: NYT Technology


Enterprise Agent Reality Check: 71% of Deployed 'Agents' Are Still Chatbot Wrappers — Claude Leads Orchestration at 40%


Jul 15, 22:24


VentureBeat Pulse Research across 101 enterprises finds that Anthropic's Claude is the primary agent orchestration platform for 40% of enterprises — more than double any rival — but 71% of organizations admit that a quarter or fewer of their 'agents' are true multi-step orchestrated workflows rather than single-prompt chatbots. The gap between orchestration ambition and reality — plus Claude's dominant lead in enterprise deployments — is the most grounded data point available on where enterprise AI actually stands versus the hype.


Sources: VentureBeat

Jul 15, 20:00


Bryan Silverthorn, Amazon's Director of AGI Autonomy, told VB Transform 2026 that Cisco data shows 85% of enterprises are piloting AI agents but only 5% have shipped to production — and the blocker is reliability, not capability. He identified four distinct reliability dimensions that evaluations routinely conflate: consistency, robustness, predictability, and safety. A case study showed an agent that worked flawlessly for two months before silently reading wrong serial numbers due to a perception issue triggered by a minor UI change.


The 85%-pilot-to-5%-production gap, explained by reliability rather than capability, is the most important framing for anyone trying to understand why enterprise AI agent deployments are stalling.

Microsoft Training Salespeople to Position In-House AI Models Against OpenAI and Anthropic

Microsoft is running internal sales training designed to position its own AI models as more efficient and cost-effective alternatives to OpenAI and Anthropic, despite its deep investment in OpenAI, according to TechCrunch. Microsoft actively undercutting its own OpenAI investment in sales conversations is a major signal about where Microsoft's long-term AI revenue strategy is headed — and a competitive intelligence data point for every enterprise AI vendor.

New Windows Zero-Day PoC 'LegacyHive' Drops Hours After Patch Tuesday — User Profile Service Privilege Escalation

The PoC requires local access but experts assess it as a useful post-compromise escalation tool that threat actors will incorporate into attack chains. The timing — dropping the same day as the largest Patch Tuesday ever — compounds the already extreme patching pressure on Windows security teams.


A public EoP PoC released on Patch Tuesday for a core Windows component means threat actors have a ready-made escalation tool while defenders are still triaging 622 other vulnerabilities.


Sources: The Hacker News · The Register


Windows Bind Link Technique Hides Malware from EDR — Creates Conflicting Filesystem Views


Jul 15, 13:00


Bitdefender researchers demonstrated that Windows bind links — a legitimate OS feature — can be abused to create conflicting views of the filesystem, causing endpoint detection and response tools to inspect a benign path while malware executes from a different one. The technique does not require any vulnerability; it exploits legitimate OS functionality to create a persistent blind spot in EDR telemetry. No patch exists because the underlying feature is working as designed.


A technique that defeats EDR inspection using legitimate Windows functionality — no exploit required — is a direct threat to any organization relying on endpoint security as a primary detection layer.


Sources: SecurityWeek


Firefox and Chrome Critical Flaws Have Public Exploit Code — Emergency Updates Released


Jul 15, 13:18


Mozilla released emergency Firefox updates patching two critical vulnerabilities — CVE-2026-15718 (invalid pointer in WebAssembly) and CVE-2026-15719 (site isolation bypass) — for which public exploit code already exists, though in-the-wild exploitation has not yet been confirmed. Chrome updates were also released in the same window addressing multiple critical flaws. Browser vulnerabilities with published exploit code historically see rapid weaponization.


Public exploit code for critical browser flaws means weaponization is hours away — browser updates need to be treated as emergency deployments, not routine patch cycles.

Jul 15, 15:30

Victims see a seed phrase prompt that appears to come from inside their real, installed wallet software.

Jul 15, 13:44

Jul 15, 11:02


A critical security flaw in the ServiceNow AI platform could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, disclosed as part of a broader patch release that also addressed significant vulnerabilities in Fortinet and Ivanti products. Patches are available and should be prioritized given ServiceNow's privileged position in enterprise environments.


An RCE in a platform that manages enterprise IT infrastructure and has deep integrations across the organization is a critical patching priority for any ServiceNow customer.

Jul 15, 16:00

The position brings OpenAI closer to Anthropic's state-by-state strategy documented in yesterday's brief. The shift, if genuine, would represent a significant reversal of OpenAI's regulatory posture.


OpenAI's public pivot toward supporting state AI laws — if it holds — fundamentally changes the industry's regulatory trajectory and affects every organization planning AI deployments across US jurisdictions.


Sources: OpenAI


Claude Flaw Automatically Forwards Malicious Prompts to Downstream AI Agents — 'PromptFiction' Chain Attack Demonstrated


Jul 15, 15:27


A vulnerability in Claude allowed malicious prompts to be automatically propagated to AI agents operating downstream in a multi-agent pipeline, enabling end-to-end attacks on targeted systems when chained with a second exploit called 'PromptFiction.' The attack required no user interaction once the initial prompt was injected.


Automated prompt propagation attacks across multi-agent pipelines are a new class of security risk that emerges specifically from agentic AI architectures — directly relevant for any organization deploying Claude in multi-agent workflows.

Meta VP of Engineering Barak Yagour told VB Transform 2026 that agentic queries hitting Meta's data infrastructure grew 30x in a single half-year period, breaking capacity, identity, and velocity assumptions the company spent two decades building. A 30x agentic query growth rate at Meta in a single half is the most concrete infrastructure scale data point on the AI agent transition — the '20 months' framing gives every infrastructure team a planning horizon.


Sources: VentureBeat


Vint Cerf Working on Internet Standard for Identifying AI Agents in the Wild


Jul 15, 12:00


TCP/IP co-inventor Vint Cerf is collaborating on a proposed internet standard designed to give AI agents verifiable identities as they operate autonomously across the open web. The initiative addresses one of the most pressing unsolved problems in agentic AI: how other systems, websites, and services can reliably identify, authenticate, and set policies for AI agents acting on behalf of humans. The project sits at the intersection of internet infrastructure and AI governance.


An internet-level identity standard for AI agents — if it gains traction — would become foundational infrastructure for the agentic web, making Cerf's involvement a significant signal about where this is heading.


Sources: TechCrunch


Anthropic and Blackstone Back 'Ode' — Betting the Next AI Trillion Is in Implementation, Not Models


Jul 15, 13:10


Anthropic and Blackstone have jointly backed a new company called Ode, which embeds forward-deployed AI engineers directly inside enterprises to accelerate AI adoption — a bet that the next major AI value creation layer is implementation and integration services rather than model development. The model mirrors what Palantir did for data analytics, but applied to AI deployment at enterprise scale. The backing from both the leading safety-focused AI lab and a major PE firm signals conviction that the enterprise AI integration market is large enough to build a standalone business around.


If Anthropic and Blackstone are right that implementation — not models — is the next trillion-dollar opportunity, it reframes the entire enterprise AI competitive landscape and changes how organizations should think about their AI partner strategy.


Sources: TechCrunch


Technology


India Announces $6.5B Smartphone Manufacturing Program and $13.3B Semiconductor Push to Challenge China


Jul 15, 14:39


New Delhi unveiled a $6.5 billion incentive program targeting smartphone manufacturing expansion and a separate $13.3 billion semiconductor development initiative, explicitly aimed at deepening India's electronics supply chain and reducing dependence on Chinese manufacturing. The announcement follows Apple and other major OEMs already shifting significant production to India. At $20 billion combined, this is India's most ambitious electronics industrial policy push to date.


India's largest-ever electronics industrial policy commitment accelerates the China+1 supply chain diversification trend — a direct input for anyone modeling smartphone manufacturing geography or semiconductor supply chain strategy.


Sources: TechCrunch


AWS Sued Over 'Water Positive' Sustainability Claims — Ex-Staffer Alleges Virginia Data Centers Quietly Consume Water Year-Round


Jul 15, 12:21


A former Amazon employee has filed a lawsuit alleging that AWS's Virginia data centers consume significant quantities of water throughout the year despite the company's public 'water positive' marketing commitments, which claim Amazon returns more water than it uses. The suit directly challenges the sustainability credentials that AWS uses in enterprise sales and regulatory conversations. The Virginia region hosts some of the world's highest-density data center infrastructure.


A lawsuit directly challenging AWS's core sustainability claims could affect enterprise procurement decisions, regulatory scrutiny, and the credibility of hyperscaler ESG reporting broadly.


Sources: The Register


Daylight Saving Time Permanent in the US — House Passes Sunshine Protection Act 308-117


Jul 15, 15:29


The US House of Representatives advanced the Sunshine Protection Act by a wide bipartisan margin of 308 to 117, which would permanently set clocks one hour ahead and eliminate the twice-yearly time change. President Trump has expressed support. The bill now moves to the Senate, where a similar measure previously passed unanimously but stalled before — the wide House margin increases its prospects this time.


Permanent DST would affect scheduling systems, time zone handling in software, international coordination, and every organization with US operations — a logistics and systems planning issue hiding inside a cultural story.


Sources: The Verge


IBM Stock Crashes Again on AI Disruption Fears — Software and Consulting Sector Rout Deepens


Jul 15, 12:31


IBM's stock fell sharply for a second time after the company previewed disappointing quarterly results, with analysis pointing to AI-driven disruption eating into its software and IT consulting revenue base. The decline is reigniting broader fears that AI automation is structurally compressing demand for traditional enterprise software and services, with IBM serving as a leading indicator for the wider tech consulting sector. The selloff follows IBM's 25%+ single-day crash last quarter when AI hardware spending cannibalized mainframe budgets.


IBM as a bellwether for AI disruption to enterprise software and consulting is a direct signal about where AI automation is already affecting IT spending decisions — relevant for every technology vendor and consulting firm.


Sources: NYT Business


Business & Markets


Stripe and Advent Submit $53.4B Joint Bid to Acquire PayPal


Jul 15, 15:30


Stripe and private equity firm Advent International have reportedly submitted a joint acquisition offer for PayPal valued at approximately $53.4 billion, backed by roughly $50 billion in committed bank financing. If completed, the deal would be one of the largest fintech acquisitions in history and would combine Stripe's modern payments infrastructure with PayPal's massive merchant and consumer network. The offer marks a dramatic strategic move by Stripe, which has long competed with PayPal, and signals that the payments consolidation era is accelerating.


A $53B bid to merge the two dominant online payments players would reshape the entire fintech landscape — a critical development for anyone in payments, commerce infrastructure, or fintech investment.


Sources: TechCrunch


China's GDP Grows Just 4.3% in Q2 — Slowest in Years Despite Export Surge


Jul 15, 11:10


China's economy expanded 4.3% year-over-year in Q2 2026, the slowest pace in years, as domestic consumption and the property sector continued to drag despite a powerful export performance driven by manufacturing. The figure falls short of the government's ~5% annual target and reflects a structurally unbalanced economy where export-oriented industry is thriving while the domestic economy struggles. The slowdown arrives as the EU prepares unilateral trade measures and the US-Iran conflict adds global demand uncertainty.


A slowing Chinese economy combined with escalating trade pressure from both the US and EU changes the global growth calculus and affects supply chain economics, commodity demand, and emerging market exposure.


Sources: NYT Business


US Reinstates Iran Naval Blockade — Hormuz Shipping at Near-Standstill, Oil Ticks Higher


Jul 15, 13:53


The United States has reinstated its blockade on Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran military conflict resumes, bringing shipping through the world's most critical oil chokepoint to a near-standstill. Oil prices moved higher on the news, with global reserves lower now than during the first blockade in April. Shipping experts warn the precedent of a toll-like regime on Hormuz passage could be replicated by other nations controlling critical maritime chokepoints.


A reinstated Hormuz blockade with lower global oil reserves than the first time is a more dangerous energy supply shock — freight rates, energy costs, and inflation expectations are repricing now.


Sources: NYT Business · NYT Business


Fintech Funding Surges 23% in H1 2026 — Fewer Deals, Much Larger Checks Concentrated in AI and Infrastructure


Jul 15, 11:00


Venture funding into fintech climbed nearly 23% year-over-year in the first half of 2026 even as deal count fell more than 25%, according to Crunchbase data, indicating investors are concentrating capital into fewer, larger bets in AI-enabled wealth management, financial infrastructure, and enterprise automation. The Stripe-PayPal bid announcement coincides with this funding surge and reflects the same consolidation thesis playing out at a larger scale. The divergence between funding volume and deal count signals a flight-to-conviction market.


Rising fintech funding concentrated in AI and infrastructure — alongside the Stripe-PayPal bid — confirms that financial services AI is entering a consolidation and scale phase, not an early exploration one.


Sources: Crunchbase News


Indian AI Coding Startup Emergent Hits Unicorn Status With $130M Series C — $120M ARR, 200K Paying Customers


Jul 15, 12:00


Emergent, an Indian AI coding startup founded just over a year ago, has closed a $130 million Series C at a valuation exceeding $1 billion, reporting $120 million in annualized revenue and more than 200,000 paying customers. The company's rapid growth trajectory — from launch to unicorn in roughly 14 months — reflects the extraordinary demand for AI coding tools globally. Emergent joins a crowded but fast-growing market alongside Cursor, Lovable, Bolt, and Replit.


A sub-14-month path from launch to unicorn with $120M ARR in AI coding tools is one of the fastest enterprise software ramps on record — a benchmark for the AI developer tools market's current velocity.


Sources: TechCrunch


EU Pushes US to Exempt €150B in European Goods from Turnberry Deal Tariffs


Jul 15, 12:00


The European Commission is seeking carve-outs from the 15% tariffs imposed on EU goods under the Turnberry trade agreement, targeting €150 billion worth of products including Roquefort cheese, olive oil, and wine. The request reflects the EU's effort to protect key export sectors from tariff pressure while broader US-EU trade negotiations continue. The outcome will affect European exporters across agriculture, food, and consumer goods categories.


€150B in EU goods seeking tariff exemption is a live trade negotiation with direct P&L implications for European manufacturers and importers of affected categories — and a signal of how Turnberry's implementation is being contested.


Sources: Euronews Business

entry.content:
PulseBrief's Afternoon Pulse


Wed, Jul 15, 05:00 → Wed, Jul 15, 11:00


Cyber Security


CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of Three SharePoint Vulnerabilities — Patch Internet-Exposed Instances Now


Jul 15, 09:44


CISA issued an urgent advisory warning that attackers are actively exploiting three vulnerabilities in on-premises SharePoint Server instances exposed to the internet. This follows Microsoft's record July Patch Tuesday which already included SharePoint zero-days, and Progress Software's confirmation of a separate SharePoint-adjacent zero-day behind the ShareFile Storage Zone Controller shutdown. Organizations running on-premises SharePoint face a compounding risk from multiple active exploit chains simultaneously.


Three actively exploited SharePoint flaws with a CISA advisory means this is a mandatory emergency patching cycle for any organization running on-premises SharePoint — not discretionary.


Sources: BleepingComputer · SecurityWeek


SonicWall SMA1000 Zero-Days: CVE-2026-15409 Scores CVSS 10.0, Enables Unauthenticated Remote Command Execution


Jul 15, 05:19


New details on the two actively exploited SonicWall SMA1000 zero-days reveal that CVE-2026-15409 is a server-side request forgery flaw scoring the maximum CVSS 10.0, exploitable remotely without authentication, while CVE-2026-15410 can enable arbitrary admin command execution. SMA1000 appliances are enterprise remote access gateways sitting at the network perimeter, making them a direct path to internal environments. Patches are available and SonicWall has issued an urgent advisory.


A CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE on perimeter remote access appliances under active exploitation is the highest-urgency patch category that exists — treat this as an incident response situation.


Sources: The Hacker News · SecurityWeek · Cybersecurity News


Cursor IDE Silently Executes Any File Named git.exe in a Cloned Repository's Root — Windows RCE, No User Prompt


Jul 15, 10:55


A confirmed vulnerability in the Cursor AI coding IDE on Windows causes it to automatically execute any binary named git.exe found in a project's root directory the moment a repository is opened, with no warning or confirmation dialog, and continues re-executing it for the session's duration. The binary runs with the user's full privileges — including access to source code, SSH keys, and cloud credentials. The flaw was disclosed to Cursor in December 2025 and remains unpatched; a malicious actor only needs to include a poisoned git.exe in any repository a target developer might open.


An unpatched auto-execution vulnerability in a widely-used AI coding IDE that fires on clone-and-open — the most common developer workflow — is a direct threat to every Cursor user working with external repositories.


Sources: The Hacker News


AsyncAPI npm Supply Chain Compromise: Multi-Stage Botnet Loader in Packages with Millions of Weekly Downloads


Jul 15, 09:16


Four compromised packages in the @asyncapi npm namespace — including the core generator and specs packages — were confirmed by four independent security firms (OX Security, SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity) to be distributing a multi-stage botnet loader. The Miasma v3 backdoor activates not at install time but when the application or build pipeline actually runs the code, defeating standard install-time scanning. Development workstations, CI/CD servers, and any environment that executed the affected versions should be treated as potentially compromised.


A multi-firm-confirmed supply chain compromise of a widely-used async API toolchain delivering a persistent botnet backdoor is an immediate dependency audit for any JavaScript/Node.js build pipeline.


Sources: The Hacker News


Chinese State Hackers Embed Claude Code and DeepSeek Directly Into Espionage Campaign Execution Flows


Jul 15, 07:18


Hunt researchers uncovered an active China-linked cyber espionage campaign that has integrated Claude Code and DeepSeek-v4-pro as core operational engines — not peripheral research aids — within the intrusion pipeline, pivoting off TencShell C2 infrastructure. The operation targets government entities and represents one of the first documented cases of commercial frontier AI being embedded directly into state-sponsored attack execution rather than used for reconnaissance or social engineering support. The finding follows the jailbroken Gemini C2 server case documented in the previous brief.


Nation-state actors using commercial AI coding assistants as core attack infrastructure is a direct escalation in the AI-enabled threat landscape — it changes threat modeling assumptions for government and critical infrastructure defenders.


Sources: Cybersecurity News


US Charges Three Russian Nationals for Running Bulletproof Hosting That Enabled $62M+ in Ransomware Damage


Jul 15, 07:45


Federal prosecutors unsealed charges against three Russian nationals accused of operating a bulletproof hosting service that provided infrastructure to ransomware gangs responsible for more than $62 million in damages to victims worldwide. Bulletproof hosting is the foundational layer enabling ransomware, BEC, and malware-as-a-service operations by providing infrastructure that resists law enforcement takedown requests. The charges follow recent dismantling of a €140M BEC ring by Spanish police.


Charges against bulletproof hosting operators are a meaningful disruption to ransomware supply chain infrastructure — the downstream effect is reduced operational capacity for multiple ransomware groups simultaneously.


Sources: BleepingComputer


White House Launches 'Gold Eagle' AI-Driven Vulnerability Coordination Initiative


Jul 15, 10:18


The White House announced Gold Eagle, a new AI-driven vulnerability coordination program stemming from an AI-focused Executive Order signed by President Trump on June 2. The initiative is designed to use AI to accelerate the identification, triage, and coordination of vulnerability disclosures across the US government and critical infrastructure. Few technical details have been released, but the program signals the administration's intent to use AI offensively for defensive cyber purposes at a national scale.


A White House-level AI vulnerability coordination program is a policy signal that will shape federal contractor requirements and CISA priorities — relevant for any organization in the government supply chain.


Sources: SecurityWeek


AI & Machine Learning


Claude Memory Heist: Researcher Tricks Claude Into Leaking Users' Stored Memories — 399 HN Points


Jul 15, 06:28


A researcher published 'The Memory Heist,' demonstrating a technique to manipulate Claude into revealing contents of a user's stored memories — personal data Claude accumulates across conversations to personalize responses. The post generated 399 Hacker News points and 190 comments, making it the highest-engagement story in this window. The attack exploits how Claude handles memory recall requests, raising serious questions about the security model of persistent AI memory features now being rolled out broadly across frontier AI products.


A practical attack that extracts stored personal memories from a widely-used AI assistant is a direct privacy risk for anyone using Claude's memory features — and a preview of the attack surface that persistent AI memory creates.


Sources: Hacker News / The Memory Heist


Anthropic Running State-by-State Campaign for Tougher AI Safety Laws — Directly Opposing OpenAI's Federal Preemption Strategy


Jul 15, 08:59


Politico reveals that Anthropic is executing a deliberate state-by-state lobbying strategy to advance AI safety regulations, explicitly drawing a contrast with OpenAI's campaign to establish a single federal framework that would preempt state-level rules. Anthropic's approach would result in a patchwork of stricter state AI laws, while OpenAI's preferred outcome would create one national standard. The divergence between the two leading AI safety companies on the fundamental architecture of AI regulation is a significant policy development.


The two most prominent 'safety-focused' AI labs pursuing directly opposing regulatory strategies will determine whether US AI governance ends up as a federal floor or a state-level patchwork — a foundational question for any organization deploying AI at scale.


Sources: Politico


OpenAI Employees Fund Rival Super PAC to Oppose Greg Brockman's Political Group — $215K Raised Against Their Own President


Jul 15, 09:00


Wired reports that OpenAI employees have donated more than $215,000 to Guardrails Alliance, a political organization opposing Leading the Future — a super PAC backed by OpenAI president Greg Brockman. The internal opposition reflects deep disagreement within OpenAI about the political direction the company's leadership is pursuing. The split is public, organized, and financially significant — an unusual level of visible internal dissent at a company navigating major regulatory and governance questions.


Organized employee political opposition to their own company's president is a governance and culture signal that matters for anyone tracking OpenAI's organizational stability and policy direction.


Sources: Wired


AI PCs as Token Bill Offloaders: Gartner Predicts Hybrid Model Where Enterprises Push Inference to Local Hardware


Jul 15, 06:26


Gartner analysis, highlighted by The Register, argues that the emerging business case for AI PCs is not local AI capability per se, but cost control — offloading token-intensive tasks from expensive cloud API calls to local inference hardware to rein in runaway AI spend. The framing connects directly to Meta's Adam Mosseri predicting per-engineer token budgets, and to Bonsai 27B running on mobile hardware. The practical implication is that enterprises may deploy hybrid inference architectures to manage AI operating costs.


If Gartner's hybrid inference model is correct, AI PC hardware decisions are now an enterprise cost optimization question — relevant for anyone modeling AI operating expenses or planning infrastructure procurement.


Sources: The Register


CXMT IPO: China's Leading Memory Chip Maker Aims to Raise $10B in Shanghai — Key to Homegrown AI Infrastructure


Jul 15, 07:29


CXMT (ChangXin Memory Technologies), China's most advanced domestic DRAM manufacturer and a linchpin in China's push for AI hardware self-sufficiency, is targeting a nearly $10 billion IPO on the Shanghai stock exchange. The offering would create a major public market vehicle for China's domestic semiconductor push and signal the maturity of its AI chip supply chain ambitions. CXMT's memory chips are critical for AI training and inference infrastructure that doesn't depend on US-allied suppliers.


A $10B IPO for China's domestic AI memory champion is a direct data point on China's progress toward AI hardware independence — the single most watched variable in the US-China technology competition.


Sources: NYT Business


ASML Raises Full-Year Revenue Forecast to €43–45B — AI Boom Demand Continues to Accelerate Chip Equipment Orders


Jul 15, 09:32


ASML, the sole manufacturer of EUV lithography machines that produce leading-edge chips, raised its 2026 full-year net sales forecast to €43–45 billion, sending shares up more than 5%. The upgrade is a direct reflection of AI-driven semiconductor demand pulling forward chipmaker capital expenditure on leading-edge equipment. As the supplier to TSMC, Samsung, and Intel, ASML's order book is the clearest single leading indicator of where chip production capacity is heading over the next 2–3 years.


ASML raising guidance is the most reliable forward indicator of AI chip production trajectory — it confirms that the AI infrastructure buildout is not slowing and is pulling significant new semiconductor capacity.


Sources: Euronews Business


Technology


Oak Emerges from Stealth with $60M to Solve AI Agent Identity — Startup Targets the Non-Human Identity Crisis


Jul 15, 11:00


Israeli identity management startup Oak launched publicly with $60 million in seed funding, targeting the rapidly escalating problem of non-human identity management created by AI agents — each of which needs credentials, access scopes, and audit trails that current IAM systems weren't designed to handle. Founded by serial entrepreneur Shai Morag, Oak is entering a market that has no established leader and is growing with every agentic AI deployment. The $60M seed is one of the largest in the identity security category.


Every organization deploying AI agents is accumulating non-human identities with privileged access and no adequate governance framework — Oak is building directly for this gap, and the $60M seed signals serious investor conviction.


Sources: TechCrunch


EU Competition Ruling Gives SAP Customers Leverage in Contract Negotiations — ECC Holdouts Have a New Bargaining Chip


Jul 15, 10:00


A European Commission competition decision involving SAP's maintenance fee practices has created new negotiating leverage for enterprise customers still running SAP ECC (the predecessor to S/4HANA) who are resisting migration pressure. The ruling effectively gives customers a tool to push back on SAP's pricing and migration timelines in contract renewals. The dynamic is particularly relevant as SAP's mainstream maintenance deadline approaches and customers weigh the economics of migration versus third-party support.


Any organization in SAP ECC contract negotiations now has a regulatory card to play — the EU ruling changes the leverage balance that has historically favored SAP in renewal discussions.


Sources: The Register


RISC-V Is Inevitable: State of the Union Keynote Makes the Case — 87 HN Points


Jul 15, 06:02


The RISC-V Summit's State of the Union keynote argued that RISC-V adoption across embedded, server, and AI accelerator markets has crossed a threshold where it is no longer a question of if but when and how fast the open ISA displaces proprietary architectures. The talk generated 87 Hacker News points and 79 comments, with debate focused on the timeline and which markets will tip first. RISC-V's relevance to AI hardware is particularly acute as Chinese chip companies, constrained by US export controls, have accelerated RISC-V adoption for AI inference silicon.


RISC-V momentum in AI hardware — especially among Chinese chipmakers working around export controls — is a structural shift in the processor ecosystem with long-term implications for hardware supply chains and software toolchains.


Sources: EE Times / Hacker News


Starlink V5 Dish Now Available — Smaller, Lighter, More Power-Efficient Than V4


Jul 15, 07:17


SpaceX has made the Starlink V5 residential dish available in select areas, with a notably smaller and lighter form factor and improved power efficiency compared to the V4. The V5 is not designed for in-motion use; a revamped Starlink Mini targeting mobility use cases was teased separately. Expanded availability will follow as SpaceX scales production.


Improved Starlink hardware efficiency and availability matters for any organization or deployment scenario relying on satellite connectivity as a primary or backup link — particularly relevant in conflict zones and remote operations.


Sources: The Verge


Business & Markets


US Reinstates Iran Naval Blockade — Hormuz Shipping Slows to Crawl, Oil Prices Move Higher


Jul 15, 10:19


The United States reinstated its blockade on Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz as US-Iran military conflict resumes, bringing shipping through the world's most critical oil chokepoint to a near-standstill. Oil prices ticked higher on the news, building on Brent's move above $85 in the previous session. The blockade adds a new operational dimension to the conflict beyond airstrikes — physically constraining Iranian oil exports and complicating cargo movement for all vessels transiting the strait.


A US naval blockade of Hormuz is an escalation from airstrikes to active trade interdiction — energy costs, freight rates, and supply chain routing decisions are repricing in real time for anyone with Middle East exposure.


Sources: NYT Business


American EV Industry at Existential Crossroads — Major Automakers Retreating as Global Sales Boom


Jul 15, 09:00


NYT Magazine's in-depth investigation finds that the largest US automakers have materially pulled back from EV commitments even as global electric vehicle sales continue to grow rapidly, driven by Chinese and European manufacturers. The retreat risks making traditional US automakers irrelevant in the vehicle category that the global market is moving toward. Lucid's near-bankruptcy scare from the previous brief exemplifies the broader financial distress in the US EV tier below Tesla.


US automaker EV retreat while global demand accelerates is a structural competitiveness question with downstream implications for the US industrial base, battery supply chains, and energy infrastructure investment.


Sources: NYT Business


Neko Health US Expansion: Daniel Ek's Body-Scanning Startup Opens First US Clinic in New York After $700M Raise


Jul 15, 10:13


Neko Health, the AI-powered preventive health scanning startup co-founded by Spotify's Daniel Ek, will open its first US clinic in New York this year and expand rapidly across the country, following the close of its $700 million funding round backed by tech investors and longevity figures. The company's full-body scan model uses AI and custom imaging equipment to proactively screen for cancer, heart disease, and diabetes. The US expansion brings a European-born AI diagnostics model into direct competition with US health systems and incumbents.


A well-capitalized AI preventive health company backed by a high-profile founder entering the US market with rapid expansion plans is a significant signal about where the AI-in-healthcare thesis is materializing commercially.


Sources: The Verge · NYT Business


Russia Bombs Odesa Port as von der Leyen Visits Kyiv — Ukrainian Export Infrastructure Under Sustained Attack


Jul 15, 07:59


Russia carried out attacks on Odesa's port infrastructure as European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen arrived in Kyiv, with Ukrainian port facilities critical to wartime grain and commodity exports coming under sustained bombardment in recent days. The timing of the attack during a high-profile EU visit signals Russia's intent to demonstrate continued offensive capability regardless of diplomatic activity. Sustained attacks on Ukrainian port infrastructure have direct implications for global grain supply chains.


Sustained attacks on Ukraine's primary export port affect global grain and commodity supply chains — a macro price input that compounds the energy cost pressure from the US-Iran Hormuz blockade.


Sources: Politico EU
